title_original: From Los Angeles to Cavaillon: The Eye of Dorothea Lange
excerpt_original: From October 6, 2026, to January 6, 2027, the Cavaillon media library present 18 photographs by the American photographer from the Musée Réattu in Arles. Cet article From Los Angeles to Cavaillon: The Eye of Dorothea Lange est apparu en premier sur The Eye of Photography…

blocks.text: From October 6, 2026, to January 6, 2027, the Cavaillon Media Library, in the Vaucluse region of southern France, will present 18 photographs by Dorothea Lange, on exceptional loan from the Musée Réattu in Arles. Among them is Migrant Mother , the American photographer’s iconic image, made in California in 1936.

This exhibition takes on particular resonance as the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art opens its doors in Los Angeles on September 22, 2026. Among the photographic works presented in its collections is Migrant Mother , now one of the most celebrated images in the history of photography.

Nearly 9,000 kilometers away, Lange’s photographs are leaving the collections of the Musée Réattu in Arles for an exceptional presentation in Cavaillon, where they will encounter a new audience. The exhibition is a rare event for the Cavaillon area. Migrant Mother is presented alongside 17 other photographs, offering a glimpse into Lange’s attentive gaze on the social and human realities of her time.
A photograph that has crossed the decades without losing its power: the face of a woman, a family and, through them, an entire era marked by the Great Depression.

The connection between Los Angeles and Cavaillon gives this presentation a particular resonance. Two institutions, two territories and two different contexts, yet sharing the same belief in photography’s ability to tell the truth of the world and the stories of human lives.

In Cavaillon, Dorothea Lange is the central figure of Le Regard en héritage , a year-long photography program taking place from September 2026 to September 2027 across the 16 municipalities of Luberon Monts de Vaucluse Agglomeration.

Supported by the French Ministry of Culture as part of the Bicentenary of Photography, the program brings together exhibitions, lectures, screenings, encounters and workshops. It creates a dialogue between documentary photography, contemporary practice, amateur photography and the transmission of photographic knowledge and skills.

Born in Oppède around the exhibition Le Verbe et l’Image , Le Regard en héritage has gradually expanded to include the municipalities and media libraries across the region. Bringing together the work of established photographers and participatory projects developed with local residents, the program explores different ways of looking: at landscapes, faces, memories, heritage and the transformations of a territory.

With Dorothea Lange as its point of departure, Le Regard en héritage places Luberon Monts de Vaucluse within the celebration of 200 years of photography, while making the photographic image a means of transmitting, questioning and renewing the way we see the world.
